preparation: issue #977 portion 1: versioned private input profile and finite compatibility/limit table; portion 2 binds this accepted profile into parser dispatch

limits.name: max_record_bytes
limits.rationale: one complete newline-delimited JSON record excluding terminator; 4x below the I7.2 4 MiB transport-frame default so frame, line and body stay distinct budgets

limits.name: max_buffered_bytes
limits.rationale: one complete record plus bounded decoder state; never two unbounded records

limits.name: max_json_string_bytes
limits.rationale: half the outer record so one large opaque string plus envelope fits; narrower field caps still apply after

limits.name: max_container_items
limits.rationale: bounds member/item explosion per array/object; narrower nested caps (32/16) reused unchanged inside

limits.name: max_scalar_values
limits.rationale: bounds repeated-member scalar denial of service with checked accumulation

limits.name: max_nesting_depth
limits.rationale: matches the shared raw-scan depth bound; bounds recursion and stack

limits.name: max_requests_per_process
limits.rationale: finite process lifetime record budget with checked arithmetic

limits.name: max_consecutive_invalid_records
limits.rationale: fail-closed termination after a short run of malformed/oversized records; a valid record resets the run

limits.name: max_oversize_discard_bytes
limits.rationale: bounded discard through one terminator; a missing terminator beyond this bound terminates the process

limits.name: idle_timeout_ms
limits.rationale: declared so the profile is complete; NOT enforced on blocking stdin, no slow-reader interruption claimed

limits.name: lifetime_timeout_ms
limits.rationale: declared so the profile is complete; NOT enforced on blocking stdin by this boundary

limits.name: oversize_disposition
limits.rationale: overlong records are never truncated into a valid request and never parsed by suffix

limits.name: host.correlation_id
limits.rationale: reused unchanged through the real Request contracts

limits.name: host.operation_handle
limits.rationale: reused unchanged through the real Request contracts

limits.name: host.observed_resource_refs
limits.rationale: opaque observations stay inert bounded data

limits.name: host.event_cursors
limits.rationale: reused unchanged through the real Request contracts

limits.name: host.trace_entries
limits.rationale: reused unchanged through the real Request contracts

limits.name: host.deadline_preference_ms
limits.rationale: preference only; Kernel owns the absolute deadline

limits.name: admitted_tool_variants
limits.rationale: explicit admission list reused unchanged; unknown variants rejected

limits.name: i72_frame_default
limits.rationale: transport-frame default, explicitly NOT a Bridge stdin-line limit

limits.name: i72_hot_response
limits.rationale: hot-response figure, explicitly NOT a request limit

limits.name: i72_structured_response
limits.rationale: structured-response ceiling, explicitly NOT a request limit

supported: UTF-8 records within all profile bounds
compatibility.notes: compatibility covers the declared bounded supported corpus only; formerly unbounded inputs larger than max_record_bytes are rejected by policy, not preserved

cases.note: blank lines are skipped before decoding
generated in-test: object with 5000 members exceeds max_container_items 4096
generated in-test: nested arrays holding 20000 numbers exceed max_scalar_values 16384 while every container stays below max_container_items 4096, isolating the scalar bound
generated in-test: single 600000-char string exceeds max_json_string_bytes 524288
framing stage reports InvalidUtf8 before decoding
rejection detail must not echo the canary correlation or body text
